# Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

> **Migrated** from the SorraAgents worklog item **SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS** (2026-11-13) after the producer approved migrating it here, accepting the re-scope and deleting the SorraAgents original. Provenance for the orphan census below is the SorraAgents worklog; the engineering scope is entirely in this repository.

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 SorraAgents backlog review)

55 of 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

`wl delete` is recursive by default (documented), and `--no-recursive` is the documented "leaving children orphaned" opt-out, but a hard delete evidently bypassed the children; the exact route that produced the 46-item batch is confirmed below as `wl doctor prune` / `foreign-items --apply` (see R1).

## Re-scope (producer-approved 2026-11-13)

Investigation of this repo (main @ `77264ee6a`) shows the original acceptance criteria are **substantially shipped**, which narrows the work:

- **Recursive delete ships.** `wl delete` is recursive by default, has an explicit `--no-recursive` opt-out, records `--reason`, and reports the deleted descendants — `src/commands/delete.ts` (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- **Doctor already flags orphans.** Root `wl doctor` (`validate`) emits a distinct per-item finding via `validateParentReferences()`: code `parent.missing-endpoint`, type `missing-parent`, carrying the lost parent id in `context.parentId` and a safe `parentId: null` proposed fix — `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`.
- **Promotion path exists.** `wl doctor dangling-parents [--apply]` detects dangling parents and detaches them (`parentId -> null`) — `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR), and `wl update <id> --parent null` detaches instead of writing `WL-NULL`.

The remaining defects are therefore narrower than the originally filed five ACs:

- **R1 — hard-delete admin paths still orphan children silently.** `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes each candidate via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`); `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` (`applyForeignItemCleanup`, `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`) likewise deletes each id individually and, although it cascades audit results and FTS entries, it neither cascades to nor refuses when an own-prefix child points at the deleted id.
- **R2 — promotion/detach loses the history.** `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply` contains no comment/attribution call, and neither `wl doctor --fix` nor `wl update <id> --parent null` records the previous parent or the rationale.
- **R3 — orphan reporting is not grouped.** Findings are emitted per child; there is no grouped summary keyed by lost-parent id carrying the count and child ids.
- **R3b — children of a *soft-deleted* parent are not reported at all.** `validateParentReferences` resolves `parentId` against `db.getAll()`, which includes soft-deleted rows (proved by `prune` filtering `status === 'deleted'` out of the same collection), so a soft-deleted parent looks resolvable. 9 of the 55 evidence orphans fell in this class.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every hard-delete admin path that can leave children without a resolvable parent (notably `wl doctor prune`; audit `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` and any other store-level `deleteWorkItem` caller) either cascades to descendants or refuses without an explicit opt-in, so no silent orphaning remains.
2. Any explicit orphaning opt-in (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment on each orphaned child naming the previous parent and the explicit decision.
3. `wl doctor` reports orphans as a distinct finding that includes the lost-parent id and the child id — including children whose parent is soft-deleted (R3b); `wl doctor dangling-parents --dry-run` summarises the grouped count of children per lost-parent id.
4. Promotion (`parentId -> null`, via `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, or `wl update --parent null`) records a comment naming the previous parent and the rationale (promote-because-live vs retire-because-stale), so the history is not lost.
5. The retention rule — promote when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is superseded, its target is gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered — is documented alongside the remediation path.
6. Automated tests cover: pruning a parent with children does not orphan them; explicit orphaning records the previous parent; doctor output names the lost parent and the children (including the soft-deleted-parent case); promotion clears `parentId`, keeps the children reachable, and records the comment.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (CLI/doctor docs and the remediation/retention guidance).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (now evidenced):** the 46-item hard-deleted batch came from a single-id hard-delete admin path — `wl doctor prune` is the leading candidate; `foreign-items --apply` can produce the same shape for own-prefix children.
- **Risk:** changing prune/foreign-items cascade behaviour could delete more than intended — mitigate with a dry-run-first default and an explicit opt-in for destructive cascades.
- **Risk (scope creep):** incidental doctor/delete cleanups discovered during the fix should be filed as separate items, not folded in.
- The delete-reason attribution defect is already fixed by **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) and is out of scope here; do not re-open or re-implement it.

## Constraints

- Do **not** re-implement already-shipped behaviour (recursive `wl delete`, the `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding, `--parent null` detach); build only the residual gaps R1–R3b.
- CHANGELOG is managed by the ship release pipeline, not this item.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` recursive-by-default with `--no-recursive` and `--reason` (`src/commands/delete.ts`; WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- `wl doctor` root `validate` includes `validateParentReferences()` → `parent.missing-endpoint` / `missing-parent` findings with a safe `parentId: null` fix (`src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`).
- `wl doctor dangling-parents [--dry-run|--apply]` detaches dangling parents (`src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts`, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR).
- `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`) — the residual orphaning route.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` hard-deletes with a "full cascade" limited to audit results + FTS entries (`src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`).

## Desired change

Close the residual gaps: make hard-delete admin paths cascade-or-refuse (R1), record the previous parent + decision whenever a child is orphaned or promoted (R2), and report orphans grouped by lost-parent id — including soft-deleted parents — in `wl doctor` output (R3/R3b), with a documented retention/remediation rule and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — cascade to descendants or refuse when pruning a parent that still has children.
- `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts` — same guard for `foreign-items --apply` when an own-prefix child points at a foreign id.
- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts` — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable; emit the grouped orphan finding (lost-parent id, count, child ids).
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — grouped orphan summary and comment-on-detach for `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — grouped count per lost parent in `--dry-run` and comment on detach in `--apply`.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — comment on each child when `--no-recursive` orphaning is applied.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — comment on `--parent null` detach naming the previous parent.
- `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — retention rule and remediation path.

## Proposed decomposition (plan input — not yet created)

Test-first ordering; each is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs):

1. **Orphan-guard failing test fixtures** (task, test-first) — shared fixtures for a hard-deleted parent, a soft-deleted parent, a foreign-prefix parent with an own child, and a promotion; tests assert the target behaviours and fail on current main.
2. **Hard-delete paths cascade-or-refuse** (R1, AC1) — `wl doctor prune` refuses (or requires an explicit `--cascade-children` opt-in) when a candidate still has live children; same audit for `foreign-items --apply`; regression tests + `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.
3. **Grouped orphan reporting** (R3/R3b, AC3) — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable, add a grouped finding carrying lost-parent id, child count and child ids, and a grouped summary in `dangling-parents --dry-run`; tests.
4. **Attribution comments on orphan/promote** (R2, AC2/AC4) — `wl delete --no-recursive` comments each orphaned child; `wl update --parent null`, `dangling-parents --apply` and `doctor --fix` comment naming the previous parent plus the promote-vs-retire rationale; tests.
5. **Retention & remediation docs** (AC5/AC7) — document the promote-when-live / retire-when-superseded rule alongside the remediation path in `CLI.md` and `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`; AC8 is verified at the dev-push gate.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** (completed) — recursive deletion of work items with children.
- **WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR** (completed) — treat `--parent null` as detach instead of a bogus `WL-NULL` parent.
- **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) — `wl delete` delete-reason attribution (out of scope).
- **SA-0MQFXG76T000A3LR**, **SA-0MW7Z1YE9004P41D** (SorraAgents, completed) — the follow-up and the 2026-11-08 backlog triage that retired the 55 orphans found in the evidence.

## Open questions

None — the migration, the re-scope and the disposition of the SorraAgents original were all answered by the producer (see Appendix).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (migration):** "Should this item migrate to the Worklog CLI project (`ContextHub`), where all target files live, or remain in SorraAgents as a cross-project tracking item?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): migrate.** Delete the SorraAgents item once migrated. This item is the migrated copy.
- **Q2 (re-scope):** "Confirm the narrowed ACs (residual gaps R1–R3) rather than the original five?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-13): accept.** ACs above are the accepted re-scope, with R3b folded into AC3. Research: recursive delete (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL), `--parent null` detach (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR) and the `parent.missing-endpoint` finding all ship.

## Goal

As an operator relying on the downtime dispatcher, I want the hydrator to treat a
live dispatch pane as evidence the item is being worked on **wherever that pane
lives**, so a claim is never released seconds after its pane spawns — otherwise the
item falls back into the dispatch pool while an agent is still working it (churn,
and a duplicate-dispatch window).

## Reported symptom (measured 2026-11-15, ContextHub)

Five seconds after a downtime dispatch spawned a working pane, the hydrator
released the dispatch claim under it:

```
01:11:14.792Z  downtime worker  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: plan) -> pane w6B:p3
01:11:15.429Z  herdr-downtime  Auto-dispatched … running /skill:plan WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR
01:11:19.468Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

At the moment of release the pane was demonstrably alive:

```
herdr pane list --workspace w6B
  w6B:p3  w6B:t2  'Downtime triggered plan finish moves … - WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR'  agent_status: working
```

and the work item was back to `status=open`, `assignee:""` (dispatchable) while that
agent kept running.

The same release had already hit this item's earlier intake dispatch:

```
00:50:37.481Z  dispatched WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR (kind: intake)
00:50:06.219Z  herdr-hydrator  released because no matching pane; previous assignee: dispatcher
```

That is the mechanism behind the repeated re-nomination of prep items: dispatch →
claim → hydrator release → item dispatchable again → dispatch, indefinitely.

## Root cause 1 — pane evidence is scoped to the plugin's own workspace, but fallback placement puts panes in the Dispatcher workspace

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:5733` and `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1758-1760`
  build the hydrator with `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` — the
  **plugin pane's** workspace (ContextHub: `w5M`).
- `createProductionHydratorDeps().listActivePanes(workspaceId)` runs
  `herdr pane list --workspace w5M`, so only the plugin's own panes are returned.
- `collectPaneWorkItemIds(panes, workspaceId)` then filters any pane whose
  `workspace_id` differs (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts:409-431`).
- `runHydrationOnce` derives `const hasActivePane = paneIds.has(item.id)`
  (`hydrator.ts:~897`); false ⇒ `decideDemotion` releases the claim.

Downtime placements that cannot use the project-workspace path are deliberately
placed in the **Dispatcher** workspace's per-prefix tab
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` precedence: project workspace + item tab →
per-prefix Dispatcher tab → legacy Dispatcher anchor). Today that is *every*
ContextHub dispatch, because the plugin pane reports
`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr`, so
`resolveProjectWorkspace` returns `null` and the fallback is used. The resulting
pane (`w6B:p3`) is in a different workspace from the plugin (`w5M`) and is therefore
invisible to the hydrator: **`hasActivePane` is deterministically false, not
racily false.**

The same trap applies to any future root whose primary placement path fails, so this
is not ContextHub-specific.

## Root cause 2 — the claim-holder backstop does not cover prep/audit dispatches

The "busy = pane OR live claim holder" protection (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU`,
`claim-lock.ts`) is the intended second signal. But it reads
`<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock`, which is taken by the *implement* work-item lock,
not by `/skill:intake`, `/skill:plan` or audit runs — verified: there is no
`child-WL-0MWFKDH78002T2CR.lock` while its plan pane was live. So for the prep tier
pane visibility is the **only** signal, and that signal is workspace-scoped
(Root cause 1). The release comment says `released because no matching pane` rather
than `… and claim holder dead`, confirming no live holder was seen.

## Root cause 3 (residual) — no grace window between spawn and pane visibility

Even within one workspace, a hydrator tick that lands between `send-to-pi.sh`
spawning a pane and the pane title/marker becoming readable sees no pane for a
just-claimed item. Nothing bounds that window: `decideDemotion` consults only
`hasActivePane`, `blocked` and `held`.

## Proposed fix

**A. Cross-workspace pane evidence (the actual fix).**
Derive the demotion signal from a workspace-agnostic pane read (or from the union of
the plugin workspace and the Dispatcher workspace(s) in use), while keeping the
*display* marker scoped to the plugin workspace as today. Two different questions —
"is this item being worked on?" (anywhere) vs "does this item have a pane in my
workspace?" (display) — must not share one filter.

**B. Fail-open when the wider read is unavailable.** If the cross-workspace pane
list cannot be read, do not release (fail-open to keeping the claim), matching the
existing fail-open rule for an unavailable dep lookup.

**C. Bound the spawn→visible window.** Do not release an item whose dispatch marker
/ claim is younger than a documented grace window (reuse the existing marker
recency concept rather than a new timestamp field if one already exists).

**D. Keep the claim-holder backstop honest.** Either the dispatcher records a claim
holder for prep/audit spawns, or the hydrator's decision documents that pane
evidence is the only signal for those tiers — with a test pinning the chosen
contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cross-workspace pane prevents release.** With a pane titled
   `Downtime triggered plan … - WL-XXXX` alive in the **Dispatcher** workspace and
   the item `in-progress` with `assignee: dispatcher`, `runHydrationOnce` makes **no**
   release and writes no `released because no matching pane` comment. Regression test
   reproduces today's exact state (plugin workspace `w5M`, pane in `w6B`).
2. **Display marker scope unchanged.** The selection-list "working" marker
   (`applyActivePaneMarkers` / `markItemsActiveByPane`) still reflects only panes in
   the plugin's own workspace — a cross-workspace pane must not light up the marker.
   Pinned by a test so AC1 does not silently widen the display path
   (`WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` intent preserved).
3. **Genuine absence still releases.** An `in-progress` item with no pane in **any**
   workspace and no live claim holder is still released, with today's comment text.
   Pinned by a test (no over-correction into never releasing).
4. **Fail-open on an unreadable wider read.** When the cross-workspace pane read
   fails/returns null, the hydrator does not release (keeps the claim) and does not
   spam release comments. Pinned by a test.
5. **Grace window bounded.** An item claimed within the configured grace window is
   never released even if no pane is visible yet; after the window, today's rule
   applies. Test covers both sides of the boundary with an injected clock.
6. **No release storm / no duplicate dispatch.** After a dispatch, while its pane is
   live, the item is not returned to the dispatchable pool: a test asserts that a
   dispatched prep item is not re-offered/nominated on subsequent cycles while its
   pane exists (today it is re-offered every cycle).
7. **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers
   (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in
   the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen.
8. **Diagnostics.** A release records the evidence that justified it (panes seen,
   workspaces scanned, age of the claim) so a future mis-release is diagnosable from
   the comment/log without reading pane state by hand.
9. **Docs.** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (or the hydrator section of
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) states: demotion evidence is cross-workspace;
   display markers stay workspace-scoped; the grace window and its default.
10. **No latency regression.** The wider pane read reuses the existing pane-list
    call where possible (no new per-item spawn); hydrator step budgets
    (`HYDRATOR_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the responsiveness suite stay green.
11. **Full suite green.**

## Immediate mitigation (not the fix)

The dispatcher re-claiming the item after each release is what keeps work moving
today, so it is self-limiting but churny — and it leaves a duplicate-dispatch window
if the item is re-selected before the running pane finishes. No manual action is
required; this is recorded so the operator knows today's behaviour is a workaround,
not correct behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `collectPaneWorkItemIds` (workspace filter),
  `runHydrationOnce` (`hasActivePane`), `decideDemotion`, `createHydratorRunner`,
  `createProductionHydratorDeps` (`listActivePanes` → `pane list --workspace`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring with
  `process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (~line 5733); `applyActivePaneMarkers` display use
  (~line 1994 in `index.ts` parallels it).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `hydratorDeps` / `hydratorWorkspaceId` (~1758-1760).
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` — claim-holder heldness probe (the backstop that
  does not apply to prep tiers).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — title builders and
  `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix` (the id-as-suffix contract the scan relies on).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — why fallback panes land
  in the Dispatcher workspace (the trigger condition).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`, `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — test homes.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — docs.

## Non-goals

- Changing the placement precedence (project workspace → per-prefix tab → legacy
  anchor). Panes landing in the Dispatcher workspace is intended behaviour.
- Changing how `pane-title.ts` builds or truncates titles.
- Making display markers cross-workspace (explicitly excluded by AC2).
- Removing the demotion mechanism: releasing genuinely pane-less claims stays.
- Retroactively re-claiming items that were released during this bug's lifetime.

## Decisions already taken

- **Keep the claim on ambiguity.** Every ambiguous read (unreadable pane list,
  pane-list inside the grace window) keeps the claim. A stuck claim is recoverable;
  a released claim under a live agent is not.
- **One filter per question.** Demotion evidence is workspace-agnostic; display is
  workspace-scoped. They must not share a helper call with a shared workspace
  argument.

## Related

- `WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH` — the Dispatcher-anchor wedge that forces ContextHub onto the
  fallback placement path (this bug's trigger condition). Discovered-from that item.
- `WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ` — pane-title-based active matching and the
  truncate-preserving-suffix contract; its `workspaceId` scoping is the code under
  change (the display half must be preserved).
- `WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` — "busy = pane OR live claim holder" cycle wiring (the
  backstop that does not cover prep tiers).
- `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` — hydrator demoting pane-less driven sessions (the previous
  hydrator over-release bug; this item is its cross-workspace sibling).
- `WL-0MVWDB7F2003SORI` / `WL-0MVWDBF71005EJM0` — claim release naming the previous
  holder (the comment format relied on by AC8).
- `WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN` — placement precedence that sends fallback dispatches to the
  Dispatcher workspace.

## Impact

An agent's claim is no longer released seconds after its pane spawns, so operators
stop seeing items bounce back into the dispatch list while an agent is still working
them — and the duplicate-dispatch window that churn created is closed.
